title: Small localizing generators for a Grothendieck weak-Serre derived subcategory
statement: Fix a universe $U$ for Hom sets and indexing sets [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal B$ be a Grothendieck abelian category relative to $U$ [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Let $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal B$ be a full replete subcategory containing zero, closed under kernels and cokernels of morphisms between its objects, and under extensions computed in $\mathcal B$. Assume $\mathcal A$ is Grothendieck abelian with its induced exact structure and is closed under $U$-small coproducts in $\mathcal B$. In the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], put $\mathcal Q=\{K:H^q(K)\in\mathcal A\text{ for every }q\in\mathbf Z\}$. There exist a $U$-small set $I$ and objects $P_i\in\mathcal Q$, $i\in I$, such that $\mathcal Q$ is the smallest full replete triangulated subcategory of $D(\mathcal B)$ [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory] which contains every $P_i$ and is closed under all $U$-small coproducts computed in $D(\mathcal B)$.

source.place: Hall--Neeman--Rydh, One positive and two negative results for derived categories of algebraic stacks, arXiv:1405.1888v2 (3 December 2015), Appendix A, Theorem A.3 and its proof, with Lemma A.1 and Remark A.2 identifying the localizing hull of its small detecting family. Archive WANTED; online source read. No Stacks tag for this set-generation theorem.

proof.text: The weak-Serre cohomology lemma makes $\mathcal Q$ strictly full triangulated. Termwise coproducts represent ambient derived coproducts. In a Grothendieck category coproducts are exact: they are filtered colimits of finite sums of short exact sequences. K-injective existence and preservation of exact coproducts by derived cohomology give $H^q(\bigoplus K_i)\cong\bigoplus H^q(K_i)$. The assumed closure of $\mathcal A$ puts this in $\mathcal A$, including the empty family. Thus $\mathcal Q$ is localizing.

source.place: Tag 06UQ, lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory; injectives.tex Tag 07D9, lemma-derived-products; source homology/coproduct theorem

proof.text: Choose $\lambda$ from the compatible-presentables lemma and put $\mathcal S=\mathcal B^\lambda$. Its clauses give essential smallness and Serre closure of $\mathcal S$, $\mathcal A\cap\mathcal S=\mathcal A^\lambda$, filtered-subobject density in $\mathcal A$ computed in $\mathcal B$, and small epimorphism lifts. These are precisely the hypotheses of the one-degree extension lemma.

source.place: Lemma A.6 and first two paragraphs of proof of Theorem A.3

proof.text: Take representatives for all bounded-above complexes with terms in $\mathcal S$ and cohomology in $\mathcal A\cap\mathcal S$, and let $(P_t)_{t\in I}$ be their images in $D(\mathcal B)$. This is a $U$-small family: choose a small skeleton of $\mathcal S$; a complex is encoded by a sequence of its objects and differentials in small Hom sets satisfying $d^2=0$. Restrict to the indicated complexes and bounds $b\in\mathbf Z$. Every complex of this kind is chain-isomorphic to one so encoded. All $P_t$ belong to $\mathcal Q$.

source.place: Paragraph before Remark A.4 and proof of Theorem A.3: the essentially small family of bounded-above presentable complexes

proof.text: Let $Z^\bullet$ represent a nonzero object of $\mathcal Q$ and choose $r$ with $H^r(Z)\ne0$. Filtered-subobject density gives a nonzero $M\subseteq H^r(Z)$ in $\mathcal A\cap\mathcal S$: otherwise its colimit is zero. Apply the small epimorphism lift to $\ker d_Z^r\twoheadrightarrow H^r(Z)\leftarrow M$. Obtain a subobject $N^r\subseteq\ker d_Z^r\subseteq Z^r$ in $\mathcal S$ mapping epimorphically to $M$. With $N^j=0$ for $j>r$, this partial subcomplex satisfies the extension invariant at $i=r$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem A.3, choice of nonzero M and initial N^0, translated to degree r

proof.text: Apply the one-degree extension lemma successively at $i=r,r-1,r-2,\ldots$. Each application retains earlier terms. Countable dependent choice yields a bounded-above subcomplex $N\subseteq Z$ with all terms in $\mathcal S$ and all cohomology in $\mathcal A\cap\mathcal S$: the cohomology in degree $j$ is fixed when term $N^{j-1}$ is added. Moreover $H^r(N)\to H^r(Z)$ has nonzero image $M$, since the outgoing terms and $N^r$ never change and every boundary maps to zero in $H^r(Z)$. Hence $N\to Z$ is a nonzero derived map. Its source is isomorphic to a $P_t$, so the family detects every nonzero object of $\mathcal Q$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem A.3, induction conditions (1)--(3) and completion of the bounded-above detecting complex

proof.text: Put $\mathcal L=\operatorname{Loc}_{D(\mathcal B)}(P)$. Step 1 and $P_t\in\mathcal Q$ imply $\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal Q$. For any $Y\in\mathcal Q$, the set-generated orthogonal-triangle lemma gives $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$ with $X\in\mathcal L$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(W,Z)=0$ for all $W\in\mathcal L$. Triangulatedness puts $Z\in\mathcal Q$. Step 5 forces $Z=0$, since every $P_t$ lies in $\mathcal L$. The triangle then makes $X\to Y$ invertible, so repleteness gives $Y\in\mathcal L$. Thus $\mathcal Q=\mathcal L$, as required.

source.place: Lemma A.1, last paragraph; Remark A.2

split_report.summary: Kept the statement and statement dependencies. Followed HNR Appendix A: common presentability rank, small bounded-above complexes, explicit initial cohomology detection and downward induction, then an orthogonal triangle. Three smaller statement-only prerequisites isolate the cardinal package, one-degree subcomplex extension, and generic set-generated localization triangle. Reused existing weak-Serre and coproduct results. No equivalence D(A)=D_A(B), Serre hypothesis on A, or compactness claim is assumed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q16-197995261 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read HNR arXiv:1405.1888 Appendix A online, since it is not archived locally: Lemma A.1, Remark A.2, Theorem A.3 with its full proof, and Lemma A.6. The item's statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint field are byte-identical to the base (side-live has it unsplit, no repair note). Its Q = Loc(P) is exactly the conclusion of A.3 plus A.1. Steps 1-6 check out. Step 1: Q is localizing via 06UQ-type weak-Serre closure, termwise coproducts, exact coproducts in a Grothendieck category and src-homology-coproducts; the empty family gives 0. Step 2 reads off package clauses (a)-(d). Step 3: elementary skeleton encoding gives a U-small family. Step 4: the base step moved to degree r, using density of A-presentable subobjects and the mono lift. Step 5: the induction, with H^r(N) mapping onto M != 0. Step 6: the A.1 orthogonal triangle, Z in Q, then Z=0 and repleteness. Each new node is true and strictly smaller than the item. The cardinal package follows from A.6 for A and B; I checked A^λ = A ∩ B^λ in both directions, using A.6(3) and that the inclusion preserves colimits. For the extension node I redid the construction: L = K ∩ X^i, V lifted monomorphically, T = V ∩ H^{i-1}, factorization through P, pushout Q in 0→P→Q→L→0 and mono into Z^{i-1}/X^{i-1} by the five lemma, then the final mono lift. This gives d(N^{i-1}) = L, H^i = K/L and the new image P, and corrects HNR's N^i index typo. The orthogonal-triangle node is Neeman well-generation via HNR A.1/A.2, with no detection or A involved. None is a duplicate: I checked lem-coef-grothendieck-locally-presentable, lem-sfb-presentable-generator-cardinal-bound, lem-per-set-generated-sheaf-aisle (Mod(R) aisle only), lem-grothendieck-derived-brown-right-adjoint and det-brown-hypotheses-generation.
